negative_findings.description: Serbian-language searching using the correct statutory phrasing (obavestenje klijentima, izmena opstih uslova poslovanja) returned almost exclusively Serbian and Montenegrin domestic banks (Addiko, OTP, Halkbank, Raiffeisen RS, Komercijalna, Banca Intesa, CKB), not Kosovo-licensed banks. No Kosovo bank was found publishing a structured Serbian-language customer-notice feed.
negative_findings.result_summary: The only Serbian-language artefacts located on a Kosovo bank domain were ProCredit's .sr e-banking manuals. NLB Kosovo, Raiffeisen Kosovo, TEB, BKT, BPB and Banka Ekonomike surfaced only sq and en surfaces in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If regulatory change reaches Serbian-speaking customers in Kosovo at all, it may do so through branch notices or Serbia-facing media rather than the web, creating a monitoring blind spot for northern-municipality payment and account-migration effects. It also risks a collector mistaking Serbian-domiciled bank results for Kosovo ones.

negative_findings.description: Searches for standalone compliance / AML / FATCA disclosure pages on the individual Kosovo bank websites (in sq using 'pajtueshmeria' and in en) did not surface dedicated per-bank compliance landing pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Compliance visibility in Kosovo appears to sit at the Kosovo Banking Association committee level rather than on individual bank sites; the banks' compliance content is embedded inside T&C and annual-report documents instead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's 'compliance pages' sub-hypothesis is weaker than expected. Collection effort should be reallocated from per-bank compliance pages to T&C version diffs, tariff PDFs and parent-group Pillar 3 disclosures, which is where the regulatory signal actually lives.

negative_findings.description: Searches in sq for 2025/2026 SEPA and IBAN migration notices addressed to customers returned CBK/press-level coverage (pre-application completed, process suspended pending constitutional review of three laws) but no bank-issued customer migration notice.
negative_findings.result_summary: The only bank-level IBAN notices found (BPB, NLB converter) relate to the earlier domestic IBAN/XK05 numbering regulation, not to SEPA accession.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms SEPA has not yet reached the customer-notice stage in Kosovo. The first bank-issued SEPA customer notice will therefore be a genuinely high-value early signal that accession has moved from legal-harmonisation to operational implementation, and monitoring should be primed to catch it.

negative_findings.description: Two target pages did not fetch cleanly: ProCredit's news index returned HTTP 500, and TEB's njoftim-per-klientet permalink resolved to the site homepage rather than the article.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both are recorded as unverified hypotheses, not dead sources — their content was visible in search-engine indexes, indicating live-but-defended or moved-permalink conditions.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A naive liveness checker would wrongly drop two of the most important notice feeds in the cell. The verification pass should retry with browser-grade fetching and treat 500/soft-redirect as retryable.

negative_findings.description: No Kosovo bank was found to maintain a dated archive of superseded customer notices or previous terms versions as a browsable list.
negative_findings.result_summary: Historical reconstruction depends on incidental URL conventions (BKT /content/YYYY/MM/, TEB Cmimorja_DD.MM.YYYY.pdf, BPB wp-content/uploads/YYYY/MM/) rather than any publisher-provided archive.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Backfill of the regulatory timeline before the monitoring start date will be partial and must lean on web-archive snapshots; forward-looking snapshotting must start immediately or the history is unrecoverable.

coverage_gaps.description: Serbian-language coverage of the private-bank notice channel is effectively absent; no Kosovo bank sr notice feed was located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Directly probe each bank domain for /sr/, ?lang=sr and .sr document variants rather than relying on search engines, which drown Kosovo results in Serbia-domiciled banks. Add negative filters for .rs domains in any sr-language query.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell named seven banks but Kosovo's licensed bank population is larger (Ziraat Bank Kosova SHA, Fibank Kosova, and others on the CBK register were found in this pass and are not in the named seven).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Derive the monitoring perimeter from the CBK list of licensed financial institutions rather than from the fixed seven-bank list, and refresh it monthly so conversions and acquisitions (Ziraat branch-to-SHA, Banka Ekonomike acquiring the Turkiye Is Bankasi branch) update the crawl set automatically.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank T&C documents state that legally valid notification may be delivered by SMS, e-mail, e-banking inbox, branch posting or newspaper advertisement — channels that are invisible to any web crawler.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Complement web monitoring with a Kosovo print/online press watch for bank tariff and terms advertisements, and consider maintaining live retail accounts at one or two banks so the e-banking inbox channel is observable. Treat web-only coverage as a partial, not complete, view of the notice population.

coverage_gaps.description: No publisher-side archives exist, so version history depends on URL-path conventions and third-party web archiving.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Begin immediate weekly snapshotting of every T&C and tariff URL in this slice; backfill opportunistically via web-archive queries against the same paths.

coverage_gaps.description: The consultations topic is only weakly covered by this cell: banks publish rules once final, not while draft. The Kosovo Banking Association's Compliance and AML committees are the plausible route into draft-stage commentary but no published consultation responses were located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Investigate whether bankassoc-kos.com publishes position papers or comment letters on CBK drafts, and whether committee minutes or member circulars are ever public; if not, record this as a structural blind spot for the consultations topic in the indirect channel.

coverage_gaps.description: Parent-group disclosure was covered for ProCredit Holding, NLB Group and RBI, but not for TEB's owners (BNP Paribas Fortis / Colakoglu), BKT's owner (Calik Holding), Fibank (First Investment Bank, Sofia) or Ziraat Bank (Ankara).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the parent-group sweep to Turkish and Bulgarian listed parents, whose disclosure regimes differ from EU Pillar 3 and may mention Kosovo in Turkish or Bulgarian rather than English.

brief: Kosovo's private banks function as a workable regulatory mirror precisely because their contracts oblige them to publish dated change notices: BPB's page announcing that a CBK regulation on basic-services payment accounts has entered into force, and BKT's serially versioned terms PDFs under date-encoded /content/YYYY/MM/ paths, are the two strongest patterns found, alongside TEB's tariff PDFs whose filenames carry the effective date. Foreign parents add an audited second layer — ProCredit Holding's Frankfurt-listed annual and Pillar 3 disclosures, NLB Group's quarterly Kosovo segment reporting, and RBI's framing of Kosovo rulemaking as converging on EU regulation — while Ziraat's May 2025 branch-to-SHA conversion shows banks disclosing their own licensing changes ahead of any public tracker. Two structural weaknesses temper this: dedicated per-bank compliance pages largely do not exist (compliance visibility sits instead with the Kosovo Banking Association's Compliance and AML committees), and Serbian-language notice tracks are essentially absent, with sr-language searching swamped by Serbia-domiciled banks. Coverage should be perimeter-driven from the CBK licence register rather than a fixed seven-bank list, snapshotting must start now because no bank archives superseded notices, and the first bank-issued SEPA customer notice — none exists yet, with accession still stalled on constitutional review — will be the single highest-value trigger in this cell.
